description: The line plot illustrates the loss ratio as a function of TFLOPs for different methods compared to Vanilla. The x-axis, labeled "TFLOPs," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1e7 to 9e8, with tick labels at each power of ten. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Ratio (%)," ranges from 94% to 100%, with tick labels at every 1% interval. The plot includes five lines, each representing a different method: Vanilla (purple line with triangle markers), SepLLM (n=64) (orange line with square markers), SepLLM (n=128) (blue line with cross markers), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green line with diamond markers), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red line with circle markers). The Vanilla line remains constant at 100% across all TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64) line starts at approximately 97% and increases to just below 100% as TFLOPs increase. The SepLLM (n=128) line begins around 96% and rises to about 99% at higher TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64, H) line starts at roughly 95% and climbs to just above 99%. Lastly, the SepLLM (n=64, H/T) line begins at about 94% and ascends to just below 99%. The plot shows that as TFLOPs increase, the loss ratio for all methods except Vanilla generally increases, with SepLLM (n=64, H/T) having the lowest starting point and SepLLM (n=128) having the highest starting point.
